title: Cycle 22: Predictive Background Warmup Scheduling
weak_spots: Adaptive warmup ran synchronously on every send, adding probe latency to user-facing TTFT
No cached winner existed between messages, so consecutive sends reran the same probe race
Background health polling probed individual models but did not run cross-provider warmup or cache a winner
ModelsTabView showed only manual warmup state, with no indicator for background cache freshness
Background probes had no low-power awareness
files_changed: rings/SR-00/PredictiveWarmupCache.swift (new) — in-memory cache keyed by (costTier, strictQuotaGating), TTL-aware
rings/SR-00/PredictiveWarmupScheduler.swift (new) — periodic background scheduler with low-power skip
rings/SR-00/ModelConfigurationStore.swift — cache injection, predictive toggle persistence, cachedWarmupWinner validation, scheduler lifecycle
rings/SR-02/ChatViewModel.swift — reuse cached winner before synchronous warmup; fall back to live probes when stale
BR-OUTPUT/ModelsTabView.swift — predictive toggle, background warmup reason/timestamp, refresh button

next_options.name: Adaptive warmup interval and staleness tuning
next_options.summary: Expose the predictive warmup interval and TTL in Settings, and auto-shrink TTL when provider health is volatile.

next_options.name: Per-conversation model pinning
next_options.summary: Allow the user to pin a model per chat thread so predictive warmup only suggests within allowed providers.

next_options.name: Winner telemetry and feedback loop
next_options.summary: Record whether a cached winner actually succeeded and use the outcome to tune cache TTL and ranking weights.

notes: Predictive warmup is off by default; users must enable it together with adaptive warmup.
The cache TTL defaults to 45s and the scheduler interval defaults to 300s; these are hardcoded in this cycle and can be made configurable next.
Chat path still validates breaker/quota state before reusing a cached winner, so stale entries never bypass safety gates.
Unit tests compile but XCTest is unavailable in this toolchain; they will run when Xcode is installed.
